text.en: In 1941 Japan's Ministry of Education gave Sakura new words, "Noyama mo, sato mo", because the 1888 ones were hard for children. That's the version most Japanese people learned; this course sings the 1888 words.

headline.en: Japanese, Spanish and Latin keep every vowel whole, where English slides or shrinks them. This course's five: ah, eh, ee, o, oo. An easy jaw and a soft tongue: new sounds come from the tongue and lips, never from pushing. A medium volume, the middle of your voice. Stop if anything tightens.

detail.en: Every vowel whole, even the last
Lips relaxed and flat, not pushed forward
